findings.criterion: Anchor executes a confirmed commission as a real trio run and the produced plan/handback is usable; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime
findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Success criteria (real execution + validated handback); Phase 8
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and then defines `absent` on `uncertainty_flags` or `human_wait` as REFUSAL—before any sample of what real Crucible/Foreman artifacts actually contain. Under that rule, if the trio’s existing journals/halts/budgets do not already emit those facts, every real handback is refused and criterion 3 can never go green without either synthesizing (banned for those fields) or teaching the trio (non-goal). A skeptical researcher would refuse this decision until Phase 0 includes a field-by-field extractability matrix over real on-disk trio outputs, with measured rates of observed vs absent. Locking refusal semantics first is deciding the verdict before reading the evidence.

findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation; campaign ledger is single source of truth
findings.section: Success criteria (fresh start); Phase 6
findings.message: Criterion 1 and Phase 6 have a spoken/typed description compile into a durable Face north-star, roadmap steps, size classes, and commissionability flags—with zero chat turns—but never route that first durable write through propose→confirm or any other explicit human confirmation. The North Star’s “nothing … written … without a human confirmation” is broader than “nothing spent.” If Face + Campaign Roadmap are the ledger, standing them up is a ledger write. As written, the plan can GREEN “fresh start” by silently materializing the campaign truth John never confirmed. Either Face commit is a confirmed act (name the confirm surface and `who`), or the North Star’s “written” clause is being narrowed without an amendment.

findings.criterion: Campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; single writer proven as a storage claim
findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 REAL-SUBSTRATE GATE; Phase 10
findings.message: D-B makes the authoritative ledger local/non-synced and says boot refuses unsupported (synced/OneDrive) paths—synced is export only. Phase 2 then makes the concurrency/crash gate required on “an actual synced Windows path,” and Phase 10 re-runs criterion 7 there. That is a substrate contradiction: either production never runs on the path you treat as the real proof (so a green synced test is a false receipt for the product), or production does run on synced storage (so D-B is false and the SSOT can be corrupted by the class of failure you claim to ban). Skeptical standard: durability evidence must be collected on the substrate the boot path actually allows—local WAL under the supported path—not on the path the product is forbidden to use.

findings.criterion: Produced plan is an artifact John can read on screen; no bespoke plan template (Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.section: Phase 1 falsify classifyArtifact; Phase 8 artifact card; Success criteria (reviewable artifact)
findings.message: Phase 0 correctly demands a live falsification against a real doc-trio “today” and to paste the ACTUAL result into the plan. The draft under review still contains neither the output nor a locked consequence (a vs b). Downstream Phase 8 already designs as if option (a) DOC-TRIO MANIFEST will honor the non-goal. That is planning on a hoped-for experimental outcome. If classification already fails, option (a) may be a new presentation template in packaging clothing; option (b) needs an explicit North-Star amendment. Until the paste exists, criterion 4 and the non-goal are both open risks, not closed Phase-0 work.

findings.criterion: Project driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD (with D-D’s proposed scope of talking)
findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 1 D-D; Phases 6–8, 10
findings.message: Success criteria and later phases repeatedly require “spoken description,” “spoken correction,” and Phase 10 “spoken correction” acceptance, while D-D proposes amending talking to typed conversational dialogue and parking speech-to-text. The draft does not apply that amendment to the criteria it will be scored against. A Stage-2 plan that still says “spoken” will either over-build audio or fail acceptance on vocabulary. Skeptical fix: rewrite every success criterion and acceptance scenario in the locked modality before claiming D-D is cheap insurance—or drop D-D and own speech as in-scope.

findings.criterion: Nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; steward compiles description into Face and Roadmap, then proposes commissions
findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 commissionability and size class
findings.message: D-C draws a WHAT/WHY vs HOW bright line, then Phase 6 has the compile assign size class, decide commissionability, and split non-commissionable steps at compile time. That is decomposition and scoping of work—the HOW of campaign structure—performed by the steward path without a Crucible commission. The non-goal is not only “no wave list inside a step”; it is that the steward must not become the planner. As written, a “smart compile” can invent the roadmap shape John only meant as raw intent. Either commissionability/size-class are deferred to a commissioned planning step, or each is justified in the decision log as still-not-planning with a falsifiable lint that cannot smuggle sequencing or acceptance criteria under new names.

findings.criterion: Roadmap shows the truth about what is running (park, restart, kill)
findings.section: Phase 4 lease liveness; Phase 9 park/restart/kill; Success criteria (honest status)
findings.message: Liveness is proven by “SIGKILL, not graceful shutdown,” plus machine-reboot/OOM variants. This draft does not define the Windows-real kill mechanism (taskkill /F, TerminateProcess, job-object kill) or how lease expiry is observed under ConPTY/supervisor topology. SIGKILL is a POSIX claim. If the acceptance test cannot be executed as named on the host the product runs on, criterion 5 is not falsifiable. Specify the OS-native hard-kill and assert `lost` within the lease window under that kill—not a Unix metaphor.

findings.criterion: Nothing spent without confirmation; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime
findings.section: Phase 7 real budget in the runner
findings.message: Phase 7 requires token/agent-count/wall-clock ceilings enforced by “the process that owns the run, not by the trio,” with halt + re-confirm on breach. The draft never names the enforcement mechanism (wrapper kill, cgroup/job object, argv flags, polling). External hard-stop can leave trio state corrupt or un-resumable; argv flags risk trio changes or auto-approve-like surfaces already banned. Without a measured, no-trio-source mechanism, this is either an untestable promise or a stealth amendment to the non-goal. Skeptical standard: name the kill/pause primitive, the resume story after budget halt, and a test that spend stops without trio patches.

findings.criterion: Nothing spent/started without confirmation, proven with auth ON on outcomes (surface already shipped broken auth-off)
findings.section: Success criteria (auth-ON proof); Phase 3; Phase 10
findings.message: The plan elevates ANCHOR_TOKEN-set tests because “this surface shipped broken twice,” but Phase 0 inventories gates and start paths—not why auth-off was the effective default (test harness defaults, missing middleware, query-string tokens, SSE unchecked, CI env). Making auth-ON the default test mode without a root-cause inventory re-tests the symptom. Skeptical researcher demand: Phase 0 AUTH-FAILURE inventory (each bypass class + disposition) beside START-PATH inventory; acceptance maps each historical failure class to a regression that fails closed when auth is on.

findings.criterion: Commission proposed for a named roadmap step; nothing runs until John confirms; confirmation records who
findings.section: Success criteria (propose/confirm)
findings.message: Citing `proposeCommission (141) / confirmCommission (250)` as “engine halves already exist” is not evidence those functions bind to a named roadmap step, mint single-use tokens, record `who`, or refuse unauthenticated spend. Line numbers are not behavioral contracts; they can be stubs, auth-off only, or free-floating commissions. Phase 3 redesigns the choke point as if greenfield anyway—so the “already exist” claim either understates required rewrite or overstates readiness. Replace with a Phase-0 behavioral table: inputs, outputs, auth posture, step-binding, and a failing test list against current code—or drop the existence claim.

findings.criterion: Real trio run; when John says start, Foreman executes; Roadmap shows truth
findings.section: Phase 5; Phase 10 criterion 3; Success criteria (real execution; when he says start, Foreman executes)
findings.message: The only required real engine cycle is one Crucible HALT→confirm→resume. Foreman blocker inventory is listed in Phase 0, then deferred as “unknown halts until observed.” researchPrime is essentially absent. North Star and success criteria say trio/Foreman execution, not “Crucible stage gates only.” A system that only proves Crucible human gates can still lie or refuse on Foreman park/restart/kill and research commissions. At minimum, Phase 10 must require one real Foreman start path (or an explicit North-Star narrowing to “Crucible first, Foreman later”) and a disposition for researchPrime commissions—not an implied trio from one engine’s approve gates.

findings.criterion: Roadmap shows the truth about what is running; campaign ledger single source of truth
findings.section: Phase 2 single writer and Python outbox; Phase 9 status_flip; Success criteria (honest status; single writer)
findings.message: Python may not write `roadmap_events` but it owns an outbox the Node writer drains. The hardening receipt covers writer WAL commit and racing writers on the Node side; it does not name atomicity for “status change durable in outbox” → “ordered event visible to projection,” nor crash between append and drain, nor Node-down while a run continues. Criterion 5 fails if the process is dead/`lost` but the Roadmap still shows `running` because outbox rows were delayed or lost. Extend the storage claim: outbox append atomicity, drain CAS/ordering, crash tests that kill either side, and projection behavior while the drain is stalled—or admit the ledger is not yet the SSOT for live status.

findings.criterion: (planning integrity for a Foreman-ready campaign that stays the SSOT for what is running)
findings.section: Intro paragraph; Phase 1–10 headers
findings.message: The intro claims a “nine-phase plan (Phases 0–3 spine… Phases 5–7… Phases 8–9)” while the body is ten labeled stages (Phase 1 = Phase 0 through Phase 10 = Phase 9). That is not cosmetic for a plan that advertises Stage-2 seed quality: wave counts, dependency claims, and “every phase serves a named criterion” become un-auditable. Normalize numbering and phase count before this is treated as Stage-1 lock material.

findings.criterion: Nothing spent, written, or started without human confirmation
findings.section: Phase 5
findings.message: Treating every gate answer as a full propose→confirm micro-commission unifies `who` and idempotency, but success criteria only name commission-before-spend and start-before-run—not mid-run gate UX as a second product surface. If Crucible has three approve gates plus budget re-confirms, John may face nested confirm stacks the North Star never described. Either add an explicit success criterion for mid-run gate confirmation (and friction budget), or distinguish “confirm spend/start” from “answer engine gate” while still recording principal—without forcing gate answers through commission_hash/step binding that may not apply.

findings.criterion: Driven by talking/confirmation; no auto path that spends or advances without John
findings.section: Phase 1 gate inventory; Phase 10 pre-answering
findings.message: Pre-answering is limited to exact sha256 match of rendered text and forbidden for the three Crucible approval gates. If those gates (and most Foreman blockers) embed dynamic project content, the optimization set may be empty—fine as optimization, dangerous if any later wave assumes reduced human load. Phase 0 should report how many inventoried gates are truly static after real renders; Phase 10 must not imply pre-answer contributes to acceptance of criteria 2–5.

findings.criterion: A project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD
findings.section: Plan overview (phases 0–3 before 5–7); Phases 1–4 vs 6–7
findings.message: The North Star’s product is the talk path, not the ledger. This draft invents a nine-phase inversion that deliberately ships load-bearing storage, tokens, supervisor, and a zero-spend stub before any durable “describe → Face → propose → confirm → run” surface John can use. A competitor that reuses the already-cited proposeCommission/confirmCommission halves and one real Crucible path would deliver the NS experience while this plan is still grepping start-paths and proving WAL concurrency. Spine-first is a build aesthetic; competitor-first would put one continuous talk→confirm→execute loop green early and harden under it. As written, the plan optimizes for not being embarrassed by a second writer, not for not being beaten by a thinner steward that already talks.

findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step; only on explicit confirmation Anchor executes a real trio run; plan returns as a reviewable artifact; Roadmap shows truth
findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 4 rehearsal; Phase 5 HALT-first; Phase 10 acceptance
findings.message: Success criteria 1–5 are an end-to-end competitive product. The phases never define a single early “thin competitive slice” that hits all of them on outcomes before the full spine is complete. Phase 4’s rehearsal is explicitly a trio STUB with zero spend; Phase 5 is the first real Crucible cycle; artifact/talk refine and full auth-ON outcomes wait until 7–9/10. A rival product ships one ugly-but-real loop (named step, confirm who, real run, plan on screen, status not lying) and iterates. This plan’s first “real” moments are fragmented across late phases, so there is no early falsification of the whole NS story—only of subsystems competitors may not need to win the demo.

findings.criterion: Anchor executes the confirmed commission as a real trio run; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.section: Phase 4 (rehearsal commission); Phase 5 (real Crucible); Phase 10 (auth-ON outcomes)
findings.message: The draft makes a continuous stub path the CI backbone “from this phase onward,” while the real HALT→ask→confirm→resume cycle is a later special proof. Competitors who dogfood the production engine early discover resume lossiness, gate text drift, and status lies under real load. A suite that stays green on a no-spend stub while real Crucible is a single observed cycle in Phase 5 is exactly how you ship “works in CI, fails when John talks to a live steward.” Real trio is the competitive bar for criterion 3/5; the plan structurally treats it as the expensive special case after the fake path is institutionalized.

findings.criterion: real execution + validated handback (usable plan artifact after a real trio run); no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime (non-goal tension)
findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Phase 8 validated handback
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and treats absent uncertainty_flags/human_wait as REFUSAL, while forbidding trio changes. An integrated competitor that owns (or patches) the engines will emit clean structured handbacks and always show a plan. This design will systematically refuse runs that “worked” in Crucible but did not emit extractable fields—so John paid for a commission and gets no absorbed artifact, only a refusal. That is a competitive loss on “the produced plan comes back as an artifact,” not a durability win. Either the non-goal must be reopened for minimal native fields, or the plan must define a degraded-but-reviewable path (raw blob + partial card) that still satisfies “read on screen” without inventing fields. As written, integrity-by-refusal hands the usable outcome to the rival who integrated.

findings.criterion: the produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read on screen and change by talking; no bespoke plan template (Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.section: Phase 1 classifyArtifact falsify; Phase 8 artifact card / DOC-TRIO MANIFEST
findings.message: Competitors win “read the plan” by opening the markdown the engines already wrote. This plan bets Phase 1/8 on classifyArtifact/buildArtifactCard and, if that fails, a DOC-TRIO MANIFEST “packaging” layer. Packaging that is not a “new template” can still be a second presentation shape John must learn while the real doc-trio sits on disk. If the falsification fails and option (a) becomes the path, the competitive experience is “artifact card of a manifest of a plan,” not “the Crucible plan on screen.” That drifts toward the non-goal edge (bespoke presentation) while losing to the rival who simply surfaces the files. The plan needs a hard preference: fail open to the native doc-trio paths as the primary read surface; classifier/manifest is secondary chrome, never the gate on readability.

findings.criterion: driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; John describes in his own words; change by talking
findings.section: Success criterion 1; Phase 6 draft-Face / zero-chat-persistence
findings.message: Industry competitors treat the dialogue itself as durable memory. This plan makes ZERO chat turns persisted a hard success criterion and replaces it with structured draft-Face state. That may satisfy E5 ledger purity, but it is a competitive risk on the feeling of talking: after reconnect, rivals restore the conversation; this restores a compiled draft and “keep going.” If the draft schema loses nuance John spoke, the steward cannot truly “compile that description”—it compiles a thinning of it. The plan never proves that structured draft fidelity is competitive with transcript retention for the NS verbs (describe, correct, confirm). Without an acceptance test that a multi-turn framing reconnect preserves every locked commitment John uttered (not merely byte-identical draft bytes), rivals win the core UX while this plan wins an internal ledger aesthetic.

findings.criterion: nothing is spent, written, or started without human confirmation; plan/change by talking; Crucible’s multi-gate path is the normal path
findings.section: Phase 5 (gate answer IS a micro-commission); Phase 7 confirm surface
findings.message: Confirmation is required; full commission ceremony (skill + seat + depth + ceiling + disk impact + step echo) on every gate answer is not. Crucible has three approval gates by design; a competitor that still records who/when/what with a one-screen “Approve Stage-1 Master Plan?” will complete the same human-in-the-loop law with far less friction. Routing every gate through the same propose→confirm surface as a paid commission risks confirmation fatigue and wrong-clicking under load—exactly when the draft says HALT is the normal path. The plan should distinguish spend-confirm (new trio work, budget) from gate-confirm (advance existing run) while keeping one ledger/who/idempotency spine. As written, ceremony parity is purity theater that a thinner rival will out-UX on the path John hits most.

findings.criterion: proposes a commission for a named roadmap step showing what runs before any spend; only on explicit confirmation
findings.section: Phase 7 confirm surface as primary deliverable
findings.message: Criterion 2 is “John knows what he is approving.” Competitors often win with a sparse confirm. This phase piles bound step, skill/seat/depth, hard ceiling, disk impact, size-class re-confirm, proposal diffs, and grasscatcher into one screen and makes answering four questions the GREEN bar. Over-dense confirms are a known competitive failure mode: people approve without reading, or refuse good work because the prompt feels like a contract. The plan has no inclusion test that every field on the confirm screen is necessary for the spend decision versus audit detail that belongs post-confirm in the ledger. Without ruthless prioritization (step + skill/seat/depth + ceiling first; everything else secondary), the “primary deliverable” becomes the rival’s easy “Start?” button in disguise—or worse, a wall John clicks through, breaking the spirit of explicit confirmation.

findings.criterion: the campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; when work runs, the Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 ledger spine; Phase 9 honest Roadmap; deferred export
findings.message: “Single source of truth” that lives only under %LOCALAPPDATA% and treats synced paths as poison is durable engineering, but a competitor whose project board is where John already looks (synced folder, always-open UI, multi-session) will own “what is running?” in practice. Export is deferred; mobile is non-goal; AWAITING YOU is in-app only. If the authoritative Roadmap is invisible whenever Anchor is not the focused machine-local app, the ledger is a single source of truth nobody consults—and the rival’s weaker but visible status wins. The plan must either ship a read-only derived export early enough that “Roadmap shows the truth” is true in John’s actual attention surface, or explicitly accept that SSOT is Anchor-process-local and weaken the honest-status claim accordingly. Right now it claims campaign-ledger truth while building a vault competitors can out-visibility.

findings.criterion: driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; spoken description / spoken correction (success criteria language)
findings.section: Phase 1 D-D North Star amendment
findings.message: The draft’s own success criteria say “spoken description” and “spoken correction,” then D-D amends talking to typed dialogue and parks speech-to-text. Competitors ship voice as table stakes on “talk to your agent.” If John’s North Star language (“talking,” “spoken”) meant voice, this amendment silently cedes the literal differentiator to rivals while keeping the metaphor in the copy. Either the North Star and success criteria must be rewritten to “typed conversational dialogue” before Stage-1 lock (so acceptance cannot demand speech), or speech cannot be a casual non-goal tack-on. Competitor pressure: do not market talk and ship type without an explicit, recorded NS rewrite—otherwise acceptance will fight the amendment, or the product will feel like a downgrade next to voice-native agents.

findings.criterion: nothing spent/started without human confirmation; Roadmap shows truth across park/restart/kill
findings.section: Phase 4 NEVER-AUTO-RETRY; lost → re-commission; Phase 9 park/restart/kill
findings.message: Honest `lost` and no silent spend are correct under the confirmation law. Competitors still win daily trust by reattaching a live session after browser blip or UI restart without a full re-propose ceremony. The draft tests detachment well but offers only re-commission after lease expiry—no first-class “reattach still-running work you already confirmed” path distinct from “spend again.” If lease expiry is aggressive (“tens of seconds”) and reattach is slow, John will face re-confirm loops rivals avoid, while still having paid for the original commission. The competitive fix that still honors NS: reattach without new spend when the same confirmation token/run is still live; require fresh confirm only when a new process would start or budget would extend. As written, liveness purity can become confirmation spam that trains John to prefer a competitor’s sticky session.

findings.criterion: steward compiles description into Face and Campaign Roadmap and proposes commission for a named step — without the steward doing the planning itself
findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 compile lint / commissionability
findings.message: D-C’s WHAT/WHY-only steps correctly protect the non-goal “steward does not plan.” Competitors’ roadmaps often include just enough HOW to make “what do I commission next?” obvious. Strict lint plus “split or mark non-commissionable” can yield a Face that is pure but hard to drive—steps too vague to bind skill/seat/depth confidently, forcing disambiguation loops Phase 7 already fears. The competitive risk is a beautiful non-planning roadmap that loses to a slightly more operational one. The plan should require that every commissioned step is not only non-HOW but also specifically proposable (skill + seat + depth fillable without inventing plan content)—a positive commissionability bar, not only a negative HOW ban—so compile serves drive-by-talk, not purity.

findings.criterion: driven by talking; nothing auto-started without confirmation; Crucible gates remain human
findings.section: Phase 1 deferred pre-answer; Phase 5; Phase 10 pre-answering static gates
findings.message: Deferring static pre-answer until after the resume channel is proven is safety-sound and NS-aligned for the three Crucible approvals. Competitors will still feel snappier on non-approval static halts during the long build. This is not a call to pre-answer approvals; it is a competitive note that Phase 5+ real runs will be chattier than necessary until Phase 10, training John on a worse product than the end state. Mitigate by allowing a narrow, inventory-hash-exact pre-answer for non-approval static gates as soon as Phase 5 is green—not only after full auth-ON sweep—so the normal HALT path is not artificially worse than the rival for months of dogfooding.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.section: Phase titles (“Phase 1 — Phase 0”, … “Phase 10 — Phase 9”)
findings.message: Dual numbering (Phase N — Phase N-1) is an internal accounting mess that would never survive a competitor’s one-pager. It does not itself break the North Star, but it will slow Stage-2 decomposition and cross-shark reference. Rename to a single sequence before lock so the plan can be attacked and built without a translation layer.

findings.criterion: A project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; John describes the project; the steward compiles Face and Campaign Roadmap
findings.section: Success criteria overview; Phases 1–4 (0–3); Phase 6 (talking Face)
findings.message: The North Star's first product moment is John talking and getting a Face plus roadmap—not SQLite, leases, or argv allowlists. This plan burns Phases 0–3 (and most of 4) on substrate before any talk→Face path exists; the talking surface only appears in Phase 5–6 numbering (Face compile in Phase 6). A bored investor reads that as building the bank vault before the store opens. Until a thin vertical proves "describe → Face + ≥1 step → propose → confirm → (stub or real) run → artifact/status," every earlier phase is unmonetized risk against the criterion that defines the product. Invert again: one ugly end-to-end talk path with stubs first; harden the ledger only on the path that already works.

findings.criterion: Full loop—describe → Face/roadmap → named-step commission → explicit confirm → real trio run → plan as artifact → refine by talking → Roadmap shows truth; nothing without confirmation; ledger SSOT
findings.section: Phase ordering narrative; Phase 5 HALT-first; Phase 10 acceptance
findings.message: There is no single early GREEN that is the whole North Star. Phase 5 proves halt→ask→confirm→resume without Face/talk commission. Phase 6 proves Face without real spend. Phase 8 proves handback/artifact. Phase 10 is where criteria 1–5 finally sit together under auth-ON. That means capital is fully committed before anyone can fail-fast the product bet. Bored-investor standard: one milestone, early, that is the movie trailer of the North Star (even if half is stubbed). Without that gate, the plan can stay "green" on spine forever while the steward product remains unproven.

findings.criterion: The produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read; real execution returns a usable handback; campaign ledger remains SSOT of what happened
findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Phase 8 validated handback; Success criterion 3
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and states the consequence: more fields land `absent`, and `absent` on `uncertainty_flags` or `human_wait` is REFUSAL. That is an honest non-goal stance—and a product landmine. After John confirms and money/time is spent on a real Crucible/Foreman run, the adapter can systematically refuse the handback, leaving no reviewable plan card and a ledger full of "we spent and got nothing absorbable." Criterion 3 and "plan comes back as an artifact" both die in production even if the runner works. The plan never names a measured hit-rate, a fallback that still surfaces the raw doc-trio as a read-only artifact, or an explicit human path when validation refuses. Without that, you are financing a pipe designed to reject its own output.

findings.criterion: Campaign ledger remains the single source of truth (durability / single writer as storage claim)
findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 REAL-SUBSTRATE GATE; Phase 10 criterion 7 re-run
findings.message: D-B forbids synced/OneDrive as source of truth and boots only on local non-synced paths. Phase 2 then requires concurrency/crash gates on an actual synced Windows path as the "real substrate," treating local CI as a false receipt. That is double-spend on the wrong machine: you prove durability on a substrate the product is forbidden to use, while the allowed substrate is demoted to pre-check. Bored investor: you are buying insurance for a house you refuse to live in. Either the product may run on synced paths (amend D-B) or the acceptance substrate is the local path D-B mandates—stop funding both stories.

findings.criterion: Only on John's explicit confirmation Anchor executes; driven by talking to its steward (usable loop, not theoretical consent)
findings.section: Phase 5 gate answers as micro-commissions; Phase 7 confirm surface; Success criterion 2
findings.message: Routing every Crucible gate answer through the full propose→confirm path (skill/seat/depth, bound step, ceiling, who) preserves "nothing without confirmation" but multiplies friction by design: three Stage gates plus budget re-confirms plus correction commissions. The North Star is a talking driver, not a compliance carousel. The draft never budgets how many human confirms a single Stage-1 Crucible commission costs, nor whether John will abandon the loop. Without a measured confirm budget (or a deliberately lighter micro-confirm grammar for gate answers that still records `who` and is single-use), you can ship a system that is correct on paper and unusable for the only human in the loop—killing "driven by talking" in practice.

findings.criterion: John describes the project in his own words; change by talking; BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD
findings.section: Success criteria (Fresh start, Reviewable artifact); Phase 1 D-D; Phase 6 deferred STT
findings.message: Criteria still say "spoken description" and "spoken correction," while D-D amends talking to typed conversational dialogue and parks speech-to-text. That is an acceptance bomb: either Stage-1 lock rewrites every success criterion to "typed talk in Anchor," or D-D is a soft lie and STT sneaks back in. Bored investor refuses a plan whose acceptance language and locked non-goal disagree on the primary verb of the North Star. Fix the words at Phase 0 or the build will argue at the gate.

findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — no bespoke plan template (the Crucible plan shape IS the template); plan comes back as artifact John can read on screen
findings.section: Phase 1 FALSIFY classifyArtifact; Phase 8 artifact card
findings.message: Phase 0 treats "amend the no-new-template non-goal" as a peer option if classifyArtifact fails on a real doc-trio. That is not a contingency; it is a licensed scope expansion that reopens the North Star mid-build. Packaging via DOC-TRIO MANIFEST is the only option consistent with the non-goal. If falsification fails, the plan must force packaging (or a narrower adapter presentation rule), not a menu that includes rewriting the non-goal. Leaving (b) on the table funds weeks of "template debate" instead of an on-screen readable plan.

findings.criterion: Steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step; only on explicit confirmation Anchor executes
findings.section: Success criterion 2; Phase 3 confirmation choke; overview spine
findings.message: The draft itself says proposeCommission/confirmCommission already exist. A bored investor then asks why the first capital is ledger schema and detached supervisors rather than wiring those halves to one named step with a hard refuse-without-token and a stub run. Criterion 2 is the spend choke; it does not require a completed event-sourced cathedral first. Building "by construction" tokens after inventories is fine—delaying any confirm surface until after Phases 0–2 is not. Ship the choke on the thinnest path that already exists, then backfill storage proofs.

findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; compiled roadmap is Face/roadmap, not the plan
findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 commissionability, size class, compile lint
findings.message: D-C draws a WHAT/WHY vs HOW line, then Phase 6 adds commissionability checks, bounded-depth split, and size class as compile outputs that the runner later enforces. That is not neutral labeling; it is work-shaping judgment before Crucible is commissioned. The non-goal forbids the steward becoming the planner. Size-class ceilings at confirm (Phase 7) can stay as spend control after a human-bound step; compile-time splitting and "non-commissionable" marking is mini-planning. Cut compile to Face north star + named steps with outcome/rationale only; push depth/ceiling to the commission proposal John confirms, or you violate the non-goal while claiming D-C.

findings.criterion: Only on John's explicit confirmation; nothing auto-started (optimization must not become the product)
findings.section: Phase 1 deferred; Phase 10 PRE-ANSWERING STATIC GATES
findings.message: Pre-answering is correctly deferred and opt-in, never for the three Crucible approval gates. Good. Still, Phase 10 packages it into the same "done" wave as auth-ON outcome acceptance, which invites shipping optimization as part of "criteria met." Bored investor: acceptance is criteria 1–7 on outcomes; pre-answering is a post-acceptance optional wave. Split it so GREEN on the North Star does not depend on, or get delayed by, static-gate auto-answers.

findings.criterion: Campaign ledger / Roadmap shows the truth (operator-facing clarity of what is running and what "done" means for the campaign itself)
findings.section: Overview ("nine-phase"); Phase 1–10 titles ("Phase N — Phase N-1")
findings.message: The overview sells a "nine-phase plan" while the body has ten phases labeled "Phase k — Phase k-1." That is not cosmetics for a plan that will drive Foreman waves and human lock gates: mis-counted phases corrupt status, ETA, and which criterion a wave claims to serve. Rename to a single zero-based or one-based sequence with no dual labels before Stage 2 decomposition, or Stage-2 will encode the confusion into the build.

findings.criterion: Nothing spent without human confirmation; plan must remain commissionable as real trio work without silent infinite spine investment
findings.section: Overview; Phases 1–4; Phase 10 final receipt
findings.message: Every phase is presented as load-bearing with technical GREEN conditions; none say "if X is false, stop and amend North Star / cut scope." Bored-investor discipline is kill criteria: e.g. if Phase 0 start-path inventory cannot close without trio source changes; if real Crucible halt text is too dynamic for durable halt records; if handback refusal rate exceeds N on dry extraction. Without explicit stop/amend triggers, the plan authorizes unbounded spend on substrate while the product criteria stay untested—contrary to the same confirmation ethic the system is built to enforce.

demoted.message: Dual numbering (Phase N — Phase N-1) is an internal accounting mess that would never survive a competitor’s one-pager. It does not itself break the North Star, but it will slow Stage-2 decomposition and cross-shark reference. Rename to a single sequence before lock so the plan can be attacked and built without a translation layer.

reviews.note: Skeptical-researcher pass only. Fresh context from this draft text alone. Severity kept to findings that would falsify a North-Star claim or leave a success criterion un-disprovable as written.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Success criteria (real execution + validated handback); Phase 8
findings.criterion: Anchor executes a confirmed commission as a real trio run and the produced plan/handback is usable; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and then defines `absent` on `uncertainty_flags` or `human_wait` as REFUSAL—before any sample of what real Crucible/Foreman artifacts actually contain. Under that rule, if the trio’s existing journals/halts/budgets do not already emit those facts, every real handback is refused and criterion 3 can never go green without either synthesizing (banned for those fields) or teaching the trio (non-goal). A skeptical researcher would refuse this decision until Phase 0 includes a field-by-field extractability matrix over real on-disk trio outputs, with measured rates of observed vs absent. Locking refusal semantics first is deciding the verdict before reading the evidence.

findings.section: Success criteria (fresh start); Phase 6
findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation; campaign ledger is single source of truth
findings.message: Criterion 1 and Phase 6 have a spoken/typed description compile into a durable Face north-star, roadmap steps, size classes, and commissionability flags—with zero chat turns—but never route that first durable write through propose→confirm or any other explicit human confirmation. The North Star’s “nothing … written … without a human confirmation” is broader than “nothing spent.” If Face + Campaign Roadmap are the ledger, standing them up is a ledger write. As written, the plan can GREEN “fresh start” by silently materializing the campaign truth John never confirmed. Either Face commit is a confirmed act (name the confirm surface and `who`), or the North Star’s “written” clause is being narrowed without an amendment.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 REAL-SUBSTRATE GATE; Phase 10
findings.criterion: Campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; single writer proven as a storage claim
findings.message: D-B makes the authoritative ledger local/non-synced and says boot refuses unsupported (synced/OneDrive) paths—synced is export only. Phase 2 then makes the concurrency/crash gate required on “an actual synced Windows path,” and Phase 10 re-runs criterion 7 there. That is a substrate contradiction: either production never runs on the path you treat as the real proof (so a green synced test is a false receipt for the product), or production does run on synced storage (so D-B is false and the SSOT can be corrupted by the class of failure you claim to ban). Skeptical standard: durability evidence must be collected on the substrate the boot path actually allows—local WAL under the supported path—not on the path the product is forbidden to use.

findings.section: Phase 1 falsify classifyArtifact; Phase 8 artifact card; Success criteria (reviewable artifact)
findings.criterion: Produced plan is an artifact John can read on screen; no bespoke plan template (Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.message: Phase 0 correctly demands a live falsification against a real doc-trio “today” and to paste the ACTUAL result into the plan. The draft under review still contains neither the output nor a locked consequence (a vs b). Downstream Phase 8 already designs as if option (a) DOC-TRIO MANIFEST will honor the non-goal. That is planning on a hoped-for experimental outcome. If classification already fails, option (a) may be a new presentation template in packaging clothing; option (b) needs an explicit North-Star amendment. Until the paste exists, criterion 4 and the non-goal are both open risks, not closed Phase-0 work.

findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 1 D-D; Phases 6–8, 10
findings.criterion: Project driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD (with D-D’s proposed scope of talking)
findings.message: Success criteria and later phases repeatedly require “spoken description,” “spoken correction,” and Phase 10 “spoken correction” acceptance, while D-D proposes amending talking to typed conversational dialogue and parking speech-to-text. The draft does not apply that amendment to the criteria it will be scored against. A Stage-2 plan that still says “spoken” will either over-build audio or fail acceptance on vocabulary. Skeptical fix: rewrite every success criterion and acceptance scenario in the locked modality before claiming D-D is cheap insurance—or drop D-D and own speech as in-scope.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 commissionability and size class
findings.criterion: Nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; steward compiles description into Face and Roadmap, then proposes commissions
findings.message: D-C draws a WHAT/WHY vs HOW bright line, then Phase 6 has the compile assign size class, decide commissionability, and split non-commissionable steps at compile time. That is decomposition and scoping of work—the HOW of campaign structure—performed by the steward path without a Crucible commission. The non-goal is not only “no wave list inside a step”; it is that the steward must not become the planner. As written, a “smart compile” can invent the roadmap shape John only meant as raw intent. Either commissionability/size-class are deferred to a commissioned planning step, or each is justified in the decision log as still-not-planning with a falsifiable lint that cannot smuggle sequencing or acceptance criteria under new names.

findings.section: Phase 4 lease liveness; Phase 9 park/restart/kill; Success criteria (honest status)
findings.criterion: Roadmap shows the truth about what is running (park, restart, kill)
findings.message: Liveness is proven by “SIGKILL, not graceful shutdown,” plus machine-reboot/OOM variants. This draft does not define the Windows-real kill mechanism (taskkill /F, TerminateProcess, job-object kill) or how lease expiry is observed under ConPTY/supervisor topology. SIGKILL is a POSIX claim. If the acceptance test cannot be executed as named on the host the product runs on, criterion 5 is not falsifiable. Specify the OS-native hard-kill and assert `lost` within the lease window under that kill—not a Unix metaphor.

findings.topic: budget ceiling enforcement without trio changes
findings.section: Phase 7 real budget in the runner
findings.criterion: Nothing spent without confirmation; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime
findings.message: Phase 7 requires token/agent-count/wall-clock ceilings enforced by “the process that owns the run, not by the trio,” with halt + re-confirm on breach. The draft never names the enforcement mechanism (wrapper kill, cgroup/job object, argv flags, polling). External hard-stop can leave trio state corrupt or un-resumable; argv flags risk trio changes or auto-approve-like surfaces already banned. Without a measured, no-trio-source mechanism, this is either an untestable promise or a stealth amendment to the non-goal. Skeptical standard: name the kill/pause primitive, the resume story after budget halt, and a test that spend stops without trio patches.

findings.section: Success criteria (auth-ON proof); Phase 3; Phase 10
findings.criterion: Nothing spent/started without confirmation, proven with auth ON on outcomes (surface already shipped broken auth-off)
findings.message: The plan elevates ANCHOR_TOKEN-set tests because “this surface shipped broken twice,” but Phase 0 inventories gates and start paths—not why auth-off was the effective default (test harness defaults, missing middleware, query-string tokens, SSE unchecked, CI env). Making auth-ON the default test mode without a root-cause inventory re-tests the symptom. Skeptical researcher demand: Phase 0 AUTH-FAILURE inventory (each bypass class + disposition) beside START-PATH inventory; acceptance maps each historical failure class to a regression that fails closed when auth is on.

findings.section: Success criteria (propose/confirm)
findings.criterion: Commission proposed for a named roadmap step; nothing runs until John confirms; confirmation records who
findings.message: Citing `proposeCommission (141) / confirmCommission (250)` as “engine halves already exist” is not evidence those functions bind to a named roadmap step, mint single-use tokens, record `who`, or refuse unauthenticated spend. Line numbers are not behavioral contracts; they can be stubs, auth-off only, or free-floating commissions. Phase 3 redesigns the choke point as if greenfield anyway—so the “already exist” claim either understates required rewrite or overstates readiness. Replace with a Phase-0 behavioral table: inputs, outputs, auth posture, step-binding, and a failing test list against current code—or drop the existence claim.

findings.section: Phase 5; Phase 10 criterion 3; Success criteria (real execution; when he says start, Foreman executes)
findings.criterion: Real trio run; when John says start, Foreman executes; Roadmap shows truth
findings.message: The only required real engine cycle is one Crucible HALT→confirm→resume. Foreman blocker inventory is listed in Phase 0, then deferred as “unknown halts until observed.” researchPrime is essentially absent. North Star and success criteria say trio/Foreman execution, not “Crucible stage gates only.” A system that only proves Crucible human gates can still lie or refuse on Foreman park/restart/kill and research commissions. At minimum, Phase 10 must require one real Foreman start path (or an explicit North-Star narrowing to “Crucible first, Foreman later”) and a disposition for researchPrime commissions—not an implied trio from one engine’s approve gates.

findings.section: Phase 2 single writer and Python outbox; Phase 9 status_flip; Success criteria (honest status; single writer)
findings.criterion: Roadmap shows the truth about what is running; campaign ledger single source of truth
findings.message: Python may not write `roadmap_events` but it owns an outbox the Node writer drains. The hardening receipt covers writer WAL commit and racing writers on the Node side; it does not name atomicity for “status change durable in outbox” → “ordered event visible to projection,” nor crash between append and drain, nor Node-down while a run continues. Criterion 5 fails if the process is dead/`lost` but the Roadmap still shows `running` because outbox rows were delayed or lost. Extend the storage claim: outbox append atomicity, drain CAS/ordering, crash tests that kill either side, and projection behavior while the drain is stalled—or admit the ledger is not yet the SSOT for live status.

findings.section: Intro paragraph; Phase 1–10 headers
findings.criterion: (planning integrity for a Foreman-ready campaign that stays the SSOT for what is running)
findings.message: The intro claims a “nine-phase plan (Phases 0–3 spine… Phases 5–7… Phases 8–9)” while the body is ten labeled stages (Phase 1 = Phase 0 through Phase 10 = Phase 9). That is not cosmetic for a plan that advertises Stage-2 seed quality: wave counts, dependency claims, and “every phase serves a named criterion” become un-auditable. Normalize numbering and phase count before this is treated as Stage-1 lock material.

findings.section: Phase 5
findings.criterion: Nothing spent, written, or started without human confirmation
findings.message: Treating every gate answer as a full propose→confirm micro-commission unifies `who` and idempotency, but success criteria only name commission-before-spend and start-before-run—not mid-run gate UX as a second product surface. If Crucible has three approve gates plus budget re-confirms, John may face nested confirm stacks the North Star never described. Either add an explicit success criterion for mid-run gate confirmation (and friction budget), or distinguish “confirm spend/start” from “answer engine gate” while still recording principal—without forcing gate answers through commission_hash/step binding that may not apply.

findings.topic: static gate pre-answer may cover nothing
findings.section: Phase 1 gate inventory; Phase 10 pre-answering
findings.criterion: Driven by talking/confirmation; no auto path that spends or advances without John
findings.message: Pre-answering is limited to exact sha256 match of rendered text and forbidden for the three Crucible approval gates. If those gates (and most Foreman blockers) embed dynamic project content, the optimization set may be empty—fine as optimization, dangerous if any later wave assumes reduced human load. Phase 0 should report how many inventoried gates are truly static after real renders; Phase 10 must not imply pre-answer contributes to acceptance of criteria 2–5.

reviews.note: Competitor angle only — refuting where a thinner rival (CLI confirm + open plan files, or a talk-first thin loop on existing propose/confirm) would beat this spine-first master plan on North-Star outcomes. Severity only where the finding still traces to a North-Star criterion.

findings.section: Plan overview (phases 0–3 before 5–7); Phases 1–4 vs 6–7
findings.criterion: A project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD
findings.message: The North Star’s product is the talk path, not the ledger. This draft invents a nine-phase inversion that deliberately ships load-bearing storage, tokens, supervisor, and a zero-spend stub before any durable “describe → Face → propose → confirm → run” surface John can use. A competitor that reuses the already-cited proposeCommission/confirmCommission halves and one real Crucible path would deliver the NS experience while this plan is still grepping start-paths and proving WAL concurrency. Spine-first is a build aesthetic; competitor-first would put one continuous talk→confirm→execute loop green early and harden under it. As written, the plan optimizes for not being embarrassed by a second writer, not for not being beaten by a thinner steward that already talks.

findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 4 rehearsal; Phase 5 HALT-first; Phase 10 acceptance
findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step; only on explicit confirmation Anchor executes a real trio run; plan returns as a reviewable artifact; Roadmap shows truth
findings.message: Success criteria 1–5 are an end-to-end competitive product. The phases never define a single early “thin competitive slice” that hits all of them on outcomes before the full spine is complete. Phase 4’s rehearsal is explicitly a trio STUB with zero spend; Phase 5 is the first real Crucible cycle; artifact/talk refine and full auth-ON outcomes wait until 7–9/10. A rival product ships one ugly-but-real loop (named step, confirm who, real run, plan on screen, status not lying) and iterates. This plan’s first “real” moments are fragmented across late phases, so there is no early falsification of the whole NS story—only of subsystems competitors may not need to win the demo.

findings.section: Phase 4 (rehearsal commission); Phase 5 (real Crucible); Phase 10 (auth-ON outcomes)
findings.criterion: Anchor executes the confirmed commission as a real trio run; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: The draft makes a continuous stub path the CI backbone “from this phase onward,” while the real HALT→ask→confirm→resume cycle is a later special proof. Competitors who dogfood the production engine early discover resume lossiness, gate text drift, and status lies under real load. A suite that stays green on a no-spend stub while real Crucible is a single observed cycle in Phase 5 is exactly how you ship “works in CI, fails when John talks to a live steward.” Real trio is the competitive bar for criterion 3/5; the plan structurally treats it as the expensive special case after the fake path is institutionalized.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Phase 8 validated handback
findings.criterion: real execution + validated handback (usable plan artifact after a real trio run); no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime (non-goal tension)
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and treats absent uncertainty_flags/human_wait as REFUSAL, while forbidding trio changes. An integrated competitor that owns (or patches) the engines will emit clean structured handbacks and always show a plan. This design will systematically refuse runs that “worked” in Crucible but did not emit extractable fields—so John paid for a commission and gets no absorbed artifact, only a refusal. That is a competitive loss on “the produced plan comes back as an artifact,” not a durability win. Either the non-goal must be reopened for minimal native fields, or the plan must define a degraded-but-reviewable path (raw blob + partial card) that still satisfies “read on screen” without inventing fields. As written, integrity-by-refusal hands the usable outcome to the rival who integrated.

findings.section: Phase 1 classifyArtifact falsify; Phase 8 artifact card / DOC-TRIO MANIFEST
findings.criterion: the produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read on screen and change by talking; no bespoke plan template (Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.message: Competitors win “read the plan” by opening the markdown the engines already wrote. This plan bets Phase 1/8 on classifyArtifact/buildArtifactCard and, if that fails, a DOC-TRIO MANIFEST “packaging” layer. Packaging that is not a “new template” can still be a second presentation shape John must learn while the real doc-trio sits on disk. If the falsification fails and option (a) becomes the path, the competitive experience is “artifact card of a manifest of a plan,” not “the Crucible plan on screen.” That drifts toward the non-goal edge (bespoke presentation) while losing to the rival who simply surfaces the files. The plan needs a hard preference: fail open to the native doc-trio paths as the primary read surface; classifier/manifest is secondary chrome, never the gate on readability.

findings.section: Success criterion 1; Phase 6 draft-Face / zero-chat-persistence
findings.criterion: driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; John describes in his own words; change by talking
findings.message: Industry competitors treat the dialogue itself as durable memory. This plan makes ZERO chat turns persisted a hard success criterion and replaces it with structured draft-Face state. That may satisfy E5 ledger purity, but it is a competitive risk on the feeling of talking: after reconnect, rivals restore the conversation; this restores a compiled draft and “keep going.” If the draft schema loses nuance John spoke, the steward cannot truly “compile that description”—it compiles a thinning of it. The plan never proves that structured draft fidelity is competitive with transcript retention for the NS verbs (describe, correct, confirm). Without an acceptance test that a multi-turn framing reconnect preserves every locked commitment John uttered (not merely byte-identical draft bytes), rivals win the core UX while this plan wins an internal ledger aesthetic.

findings.section: Phase 5 (gate answer IS a micro-commission); Phase 7 confirm surface
findings.criterion: nothing is spent, written, or started without human confirmation; plan/change by talking; Crucible’s multi-gate path is the normal path
findings.message: Confirmation is required; full commission ceremony (skill + seat + depth + ceiling + disk impact + step echo) on every gate answer is not. Crucible has three approval gates by design; a competitor that still records who/when/what with a one-screen “Approve Stage-1 Master Plan?” will complete the same human-in-the-loop law with far less friction. Routing every gate through the same propose→confirm surface as a paid commission risks confirmation fatigue and wrong-clicking under load—exactly when the draft says HALT is the normal path. The plan should distinguish spend-confirm (new trio work, budget) from gate-confirm (advance existing run) while keeping one ledger/who/idempotency spine. As written, ceremony parity is purity theater that a thinner rival will out-UX on the path John hits most.

findings.topic: confirm surface density vs clear spend decision
findings.section: Phase 7 confirm surface as primary deliverable
findings.criterion: proposes a commission for a named roadmap step showing what runs before any spend; only on explicit confirmation
findings.message: Criterion 2 is “John knows what he is approving.” Competitors often win with a sparse confirm. This phase piles bound step, skill/seat/depth, hard ceiling, disk impact, size-class re-confirm, proposal diffs, and grasscatcher into one screen and makes answering four questions the GREEN bar. Over-dense confirms are a known competitive failure mode: people approve without reading, or refuse good work because the prompt feels like a contract. The plan has no inclusion test that every field on the confirm screen is necessary for the spend decision versus audit detail that belongs post-confirm in the ledger. Without ruthless prioritization (step + skill/seat/depth + ceiling first; everything else secondary), the “primary deliverable” becomes the rival’s easy “Start?” button in disguise—or worse, a wall John clicks through, breaking the spirit of explicit confirmation.

findings.topic: local-only ledger vs visible campaign truth
findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 ledger spine; Phase 9 honest Roadmap; deferred export
findings.criterion: the campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; when work runs, the Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: “Single source of truth” that lives only under %LOCALAPPDATA% and treats synced paths as poison is durable engineering, but a competitor whose project board is where John already looks (synced folder, always-open UI, multi-session) will own “what is running?” in practice. Export is deferred; mobile is non-goal; AWAITING YOU is in-app only. If the authoritative Roadmap is invisible whenever Anchor is not the focused machine-local app, the ledger is a single source of truth nobody consults—and the rival’s weaker but visible status wins. The plan must either ship a read-only derived export early enough that “Roadmap shows the truth” is true in John’s actual attention surface, or explicitly accept that SSOT is Anchor-process-local and weaken the honest-status claim accordingly. Right now it claims campaign-ledger truth while building a vault competitors can out-visibility.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-D North Star amendment
findings.criterion: driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; spoken description / spoken correction (success criteria language)
findings.message: The draft’s own success criteria say “spoken description” and “spoken correction,” then D-D amends talking to typed dialogue and parks speech-to-text. Competitors ship voice as table stakes on “talk to your agent.” If John’s North Star language (“talking,” “spoken”) meant voice, this amendment silently cedes the literal differentiator to rivals while keeping the metaphor in the copy. Either the North Star and success criteria must be rewritten to “typed conversational dialogue” before Stage-1 lock (so acceptance cannot demand speech), or speech cannot be a casual non-goal tack-on. Competitor pressure: do not market talk and ship type without an explicit, recorded NS rewrite—otherwise acceptance will fight the amendment, or the product will feel like a downgrade next to voice-native agents.

findings.section: Phase 4 NEVER-AUTO-RETRY; lost → re-commission; Phase 9 park/restart/kill
findings.criterion: nothing spent/started without human confirmation; Roadmap shows truth across park/restart/kill
findings.message: Honest `lost` and no silent spend are correct under the confirmation law. Competitors still win daily trust by reattaching a live session after browser blip or UI restart without a full re-propose ceremony. The draft tests detachment well but offers only re-commission after lease expiry—no first-class “reattach still-running work you already confirmed” path distinct from “spend again.” If lease expiry is aggressive (“tens of seconds”) and reattach is slow, John will face re-confirm loops rivals avoid, while still having paid for the original commission. The competitive fix that still honors NS: reattach without new spend when the same confirmation token/run is still live; require fresh confirm only when a new process would start or budget would extend. As written, liveness purity can become confirmation spam that trains John to prefer a competitor’s sticky session.

findings.topic: compile brightness vs useful roadmap rival
findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 compile lint / commissionability
findings.criterion: steward compiles description into Face and Campaign Roadmap and proposes commission for a named step — without the steward doing the planning itself
findings.message: D-C’s WHAT/WHY-only steps correctly protect the non-goal “steward does not plan.” Competitors’ roadmaps often include just enough HOW to make “what do I commission next?” obvious. Strict lint plus “split or mark non-commissionable” can yield a Face that is pure but hard to drive—steps too vague to bind skill/seat/depth confidently, forcing disambiguation loops Phase 7 already fears. The competitive risk is a beautiful non-planning roadmap that loses to a slightly more operational one. The plan should require that every commissioned step is not only non-HOW but also specifically proposable (skill + seat + depth fillable without inventing plan content)—a positive commissionability bar, not only a negative HOW ban—so compile serves drive-by-talk, not purity.

findings.topic: pre-answer deferral vs gate-chatty rival experience
findings.section: Phase 1 deferred pre-answer; Phase 5; Phase 10 pre-answering static gates
findings.criterion: driven by talking; nothing auto-started without confirmation; Crucible gates remain human
findings.message: Deferring static pre-answer until after the resume channel is proven is safety-sound and NS-aligned for the three Crucible approvals. Competitors will still feel snappier on non-approval static halts during the long build. This is not a call to pre-answer approvals; it is a competitive note that Phase 5+ real runs will be chattier than necessary until Phase 10, training John on a worse product than the end state. Mitigate by allowing a narrow, inventory-hash-exact pre-answer for non-approval static gates as soon as Phase 5 is green—not only after full auth-ON sweep—so the normal HALT path is not artificially worse than the rival for months of dogfooding.

findings.topic: phase numbering vs competitor onboarding clarity
findings.section: Phase titles (“Phase 1 — Phase 0”, … “Phase 10 — Phase 9”)
findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: Dual numbering (Phase N — Phase N-1) is an internal accounting mess that would never survive a competitor’s one-pager. It does not itself break the North Star, but it will slow Stage-2 decomposition and cross-shark reference. Rename to a single sequence before lock so the plan can be attacked and built without a translation layer.

reviews.note: Analyst Shark, bored-investor angle. Findings only where capital, time-to-value, or false receipts threaten a North-Star criterion. Infrastructure polish that does not change John's "talk → confirm → truth" loop is demoted or left unraised.

findings.topic: product value deferred behind infrastructure spine
findings.section: Success criteria overview; Phases 1–4 (0–3); Phase 6 (talking Face)
findings.criterion: A project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; John describes the project; the steward compiles Face and Campaign Roadmap
findings.message: The North Star's first product moment is John talking and getting a Face plus roadmap—not SQLite, leases, or argv allowlists. This plan burns Phases 0–3 (and most of 4) on substrate before any talk→Face path exists; the talking surface only appears in Phase 5–6 numbering (Face compile in Phase 6). A bored investor reads that as building the bank vault before the store opens. Until a thin vertical proves "describe → Face + ≥1 step → propose → confirm → (stub or real) run → artifact/status," every earlier phase is unmonetized risk against the criterion that defines the product. Invert again: one ugly end-to-end talk path with stubs first; harden the ledger only on the path that already works.

findings.topic: no early end-to-end North-Star demo gate
findings.section: Phase ordering narrative; Phase 5 HALT-first; Phase 10 acceptance
findings.criterion: Full loop—describe → Face/roadmap → named-step commission → explicit confirm → real trio run → plan as artifact → refine by talking → Roadmap shows truth; nothing without confirmation; ledger SSOT
findings.message: There is no single early GREEN that is the whole North Star. Phase 5 proves halt→ask→confirm→resume without Face/talk commission. Phase 6 proves Face without real spend. Phase 8 proves handback/artifact. Phase 10 is where criteria 1–5 finally sit together under auth-ON. That means capital is fully committed before anyone can fail-fast the product bet. Bored-investor standard: one milestone, early, that is the movie trailer of the North Star (even if half is stubbed). Without that gate, the plan can stay "green" on spine forever while the steward product remains unproven.

findings.topic: handback refusal cascade after real spend
findings.section: Phase 1 D-A; Phase 8 validated handback; Success criterion 3
findings.criterion: The produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read; real execution returns a usable handback; campaign ledger remains SSOT of what happened
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and states the consequence: more fields land `absent`, and `absent` on `uncertainty_flags` or `human_wait` is REFUSAL. That is an honest non-goal stance—and a product landmine. After John confirms and money/time is spent on a real Crucible/Foreman run, the adapter can systematically refuse the handback, leaving no reviewable plan card and a ledger full of "we spent and got nothing absorbable." Criterion 3 and "plan comes back as an artifact" both die in production even if the runner works. The plan never names a measured hit-rate, a fallback that still surfaces the raw doc-trio as a read-only artifact, or an explicit human path when validation refuses. Without that, you are financing a pipe designed to reject its own output.

findings.topic: real-substrate test vs local-only ledger contradiction
findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 REAL-SUBSTRATE GATE; Phase 10 criterion 7 re-run
findings.criterion: Campaign ledger remains the single source of truth (durability / single writer as storage claim)
findings.message: D-B forbids synced/OneDrive as source of truth and boots only on local non-synced paths. Phase 2 then requires concurrency/crash gates on an actual synced Windows path as the "real substrate," treating local CI as a false receipt. That is double-spend on the wrong machine: you prove durability on a substrate the product is forbidden to use, while the allowed substrate is demoted to pre-check. Bored investor: you are buying insurance for a house you refuse to live in. Either the product may run on synced paths (amend D-B) or the acceptance substrate is the local path D-B mandates—stop funding both stories.

findings.topic: confirm friction multiplies at every gate
findings.section: Phase 5 gate answers as micro-commissions; Phase 7 confirm surface; Success criterion 2
findings.criterion: Only on John's explicit confirmation Anchor executes; driven by talking to its steward (usable loop, not theoretical consent)
findings.message: Routing every Crucible gate answer through the full propose→confirm path (skill/seat/depth, bound step, ceiling, who) preserves "nothing without confirmation" but multiplies friction by design: three Stage gates plus budget re-confirms plus correction commissions. The North Star is a talking driver, not a compliance carousel. The draft never budgets how many human confirms a single Stage-1 Crucible commission costs, nor whether John will abandon the loop. Without a measured confirm budget (or a deliberately lighter micro-confirm grammar for gate answers that still records `who` and is single-use), you can ship a system that is correct on paper and unusable for the only human in the loop—killing "driven by talking" in practice.

findings.topic: spoken success criteria vs typed-only amendment
findings.section: Success criteria (Fresh start, Reviewable artifact); Phase 1 D-D; Phase 6 deferred STT
findings.criterion: John describes the project in his own words; change by talking; BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD
findings.message: Criteria still say "spoken description" and "spoken correction," while D-D amends talking to typed conversational dialogue and parks speech-to-text. That is an acceptance bomb: either Stage-1 lock rewrites every success criterion to "typed talk in Anchor," or D-D is a soft lie and STT sneaks back in. Bored investor refuses a plan whose acceptance language and locked non-goal disagree on the primary verb of the North Star. Fix the words at Phase 0 or the build will argue at the gate.

findings.section: Phase 1 FALSIFY classifyArtifact; Phase 8 artifact card
findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — no bespoke plan template (the Crucible plan shape IS the template); plan comes back as artifact John can read on screen
findings.message: Phase 0 treats "amend the no-new-template non-goal" as a peer option if classifyArtifact fails on a real doc-trio. That is not a contingency; it is a licensed scope expansion that reopens the North Star mid-build. Packaging via DOC-TRIO MANIFEST is the only option consistent with the non-goal. If falsification fails, the plan must force packaging (or a narrower adapter presentation rule), not a menu that includes rewriting the non-goal. Leaving (b) on the table funds weeks of "template debate" instead of an on-screen readable plan.

findings.topic: existing propose/confirm halves unused for early ship
findings.section: Success criterion 2; Phase 3 confirmation choke; overview spine
findings.criterion: Steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step; only on explicit confirmation Anchor executes
findings.message: The draft itself says proposeCommission/confirmCommission already exist. A bored investor then asks why the first capital is ledger schema and detached supervisors rather than wiring those halves to one named step with a hard refuse-without-token and a stub run. Criterion 2 is the spend choke; it does not require a completed event-sourced cathedral first. Building "by construction" tokens after inventories is fine—delaying any confirm surface until after Phases 0–2 is not. Ship the choke on the thinnest path that already exists, then backfill storage proofs.

findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 commissionability, size class, compile lint
findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; compiled roadmap is Face/roadmap, not the plan
findings.message: D-C draws a WHAT/WHY vs HOW line, then Phase 6 adds commissionability checks, bounded-depth split, and size class as compile outputs that the runner later enforces. That is not neutral labeling; it is work-shaping judgment before Crucible is commissioned. The non-goal forbids the steward becoming the planner. Size-class ceilings at confirm (Phase 7) can stay as spend control after a human-bound step; compile-time splitting and "non-commissionable" marking is mini-planning. Cut compile to Face north star + named steps with outcome/rationale only; push depth/ceiling to the commission proposal John confirms, or you violate the non-goal while claiming D-C.

findings.section: Phase 1 deferred; Phase 10 PRE-ANSWERING STATIC GATES
findings.criterion: Only on John's explicit confirmation; nothing auto-started (optimization must not become the product)
findings.message: Pre-answering is correctly deferred and opt-in, never for the three Crucible approval gates. Good. Still, Phase 10 packages it into the same "done" wave as auth-ON outcome acceptance, which invites shipping optimization as part of "criteria met." Bored investor: acceptance is criteria 1–7 on outcomes; pre-answering is a post-acceptance optional wave. Split it so GREEN on the North Star does not depend on, or get delayed by, static-gate auto-answers.

findings.section: Overview ("nine-phase"); Phase 1–10 titles ("Phase N — Phase N-1")
findings.criterion: Campaign ledger / Roadmap shows the truth (operator-facing clarity of what is running and what "done" means for the campaign itself)
findings.message: The overview sells a "nine-phase plan" while the body has ten phases labeled "Phase k — Phase k-1." That is not cosmetics for a plan that will drive Foreman waves and human lock gates: mis-counted phases corrupt status, ETA, and which criterion a wave claims to serve. Rename to a single zero-based or one-based sequence with no dual labels before Stage 2 decomposition, or Stage-2 will encode the confusion into the build.

findings.topic: no capital kill criteria on spine phases
findings.section: Overview; Phases 1–4; Phase 10 final receipt
findings.criterion: Nothing spent without human confirmation; plan must remain commissionable as real trio work without silent infinite spine investment
findings.message: Every phase is presented as load-bearing with technical GREEN conditions; none say "if X is false, stop and amend North Star / cut scope." Bored-investor discipline is kill criteria: e.g. if Phase 0 start-path inventory cannot close without trio source changes; if real Crucible halt text is too dynamic for durable halt records; if handback refusal rate exceeds N on dry extraction. Without explicit stop/amend triggers, the plan authorizes unbounded spend on substrate while the product criteria stay untested—contrary to the same confirmation ethic the system is built to enforce.
